description: PHYSICALITY - STRENGTH DECIDES MORE OF A DUEL. WHAT CHANGES: when two bodies overlap, 0x144310ea0 returns each player's SHARE of the separation - low means he holds his ground, high means he gets shoved (the caller does accum += direction * overlap * ratio, and the two players' ratios provably sum to exactly 1.0). For an open duel (nobody holding the ball, which includes every loose ball and every 50/50) the formula is ret = 0.5 - 0.35*speedSkew - 0.3*(1 - 0.5*|speedSkew|)*T, where T = clamp(accumulator, -W, +W) / W and W is 30. This pack narrows W to 25, so the terms inside the window bite about 1.2x harder before saturating. WHAT THE WINDOW ACTUALLY CLAMPS - corrected this pass, and it matters. The clamped quantity is NOT the raw Physical Contact gap. It is an accumulator: each player's attribute 0x29 (fetched at 0x1443111a1 and 0x144311226, defaulting to 40 when the slot is out of range), plus a +5 skill term (xmm12, added at 0x14431120f and 0x144311294), plus a conditional +10 (cell 0x145a8dd7c, added at 0x144311441 and 0x144311454); the two are subtracted at 0x1443114a3, and THEN a facing term of -15 (xmm8, loaded at 0x1443112b0) or +15 (0x14431155c) is folded in before the clamp. So narrowing W amplifies all of those by the same factor, not just strength. That is why W is 25 here and not the 20 this pack was first drafted with: at W=20 the +/-15 facing term alone fills 75% of the window, so any duel where it fires saturates on a 5-point strength gap and strength stops mattering beyond that - the opposite of the goal. At W=25 the facing term is 60% of the window and a 10-point gap still moves the result. WHO IT AFFECTS: everyone - the human's player, his AI team-mates and the CPU, symmetrically. EVIDENCE: DEMONSTRATED (level a). I re-ran the Unicorn harness on the pristine image this pass with the two re-aims applied as an emulation-only overlay. Numbers are the value returned for the player the code calls SELF; at A=80 B=70 that value is 0.400, so it is the STRONGER man's share, and the weaker man gets 1 minus it. (The earlier draft and its report both labelled this 'the weaker man's share'. That was backwards.) Stronger man's share, stock -> W=25: 75v70 .450 -> .440, 80v70 .400 -> .380, 85v70 .350 -> .320, 90v70 .300 -> .260, 95v70 .250 -> .200. Gaps of 25+ points saturate at .200, unchanged. (For reference, W=20 would give 80v70 .350, 90v70 .200 - and would saturate everything from 20 points up.) Symmetry still holds exactly: the two players' ratios sum to 1.0000 at 80v70, 90v60 and 99v40. The output range is provably unchanged, because the clamp and the divisor move together so |T| <= 1 either way - I confirmed stock and W=25 give the identical extremes (1.0000 and 0.0000) at every speed skew tested, which matters because the caller does an exact equality test against 1.0 at 0x1441098f8. The ball-holder path is untouched (80v70 stays .4667 either way). INFERRED ONLY (level c): the attribute naming, index 0x29 = Physical Contact, taken from usage context rather than the game's attribute table. THE TWO EDITS MUST BE APPLIED TOGETHER: one load at 0x14431156e feeds BOTH the minss at 0x144311591 and the divss at 0x1443115ab, and a separate load at 0x144311576 holds the lower clamp for the maxss at 0x144311589. Re-aiming only one would leave an asymmetric window favouring whichever player the code calls 'self'. WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN A MATCH: a big centre-half winning a shoulder-to-shoulder against a 70-strength forward instead of the two bouncing off each other; loose-ball scrambles going to the stronger body more often. Momentum still outweighs strength in an open duel (equal strength with one man arriving at 20 km/h gives .850/.150), which is realistic and is left alone. NOT INCLUDED, DELIBERATELY: the ball-holder's automatic protection. The branch at 0x14431145b routes any duel involving the carrier down a compressed strength-only formula that ignores momentum entirely (emulated: a defender arriving at 0, 10, 20 or 30 km/h all give exactly .5000). Removing it needs an opcode edit (74 -> EB), which is outside the rules this pack set was authored under - it is one byte and fully emulated, but it needs your explicit call. STRONGER VERSION: W=20 - re-aim 0x14431156e to cell 0x145a8aa44 = 20.0 (bytes F30F100DCE947701) and 0x144311576 to cell 0x146affd44 = -20.0 (bytes F30F1005C6E77E02), both together. Read the facing-term paragraph above before you do. Do NOT instead raise the 0.3 coefficient at 0x1443116fa: the constants are tuned so 0.35 + 0.3*0.5 = 0.5, there is no clamp on the return, and raising it would push the result past 1.0 into that equality test. REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/phys-duel-strength.json

patches.name: saturation window upper bound and divisor 30 -> 25
patches.note: movss xmm1, [0x145a8dd80 = 30.0] re-aimed to [0x145da7de0 = 25.0]. This one load feeds BOTH the minss at 0x144311591 and the divss at 0x1443115ab. Target cell .tls$, writers=0, ptr_refs=0.

patches.name: saturation window lower bound -30 -> -25
patches.note: movss xmm0, [0x146affd48 = -30.0] re-aimed to [0x146b01d94 = -25.0]; feeds the maxss at 0x144311589. Must move with the edit above. Target cell .tls$, writers=0, ptr_refs=0.
